body: Possibly similar / same issue as #3819 (which I only found after creating this)

Can you try this so we can see the HTTP transaction. rclone mkdir REDACTED:/REDACTED-backups/RE/DA/CT/ED/ -vv --retries 1 --low-level-retries 1 --dump bodies Does the user have permission to create buckets? Rclone tries to create the bucket as a shorthand for see if the bucket exists, create it if it doesn't. It relies on the error codes returned from the API which I guess may be different for wasabi. You can almost certainly work around this with --s3-no-check-bucket If set, don't attempt to check the bucket exists or create it However I'd like to get to the bottom of this! user does not have permissions to create a bucket. However the bucket already exists so they don't need that permission, and it works with v1.47.0. It has permissions to create folders and files within the bucket, but not to delete them which is what we require for this key / secret pair. It's entirely possible Wasabi is either "incompatible" or at least different to AWS S3 - unfortunately I don't know S3 well enough to comment on that. I can tell you the same operation using the same key / secret pair works fine using CyberDuck 7.5.2 using "Amazon S3" settings, and it works using rclone 1.47.0. So as a wise boss of mine used to say "what changed?" between 1.47.0 and 1.52.2 - that's where I'd look. For now I've downgraded everything to rclone 1.47.0 (and modified our install process to install only 1.47.0) because that's easier and quicker than upgrading everything and trying to get it to work. As this is all scripted and the script is the shared across all machines we need one set of config / commands to work for everything. We don't need any new things, so 1.47.0 is fine for us for now. However, I'd like to help you get to the bottom of this and iron out whatever that breaking change is. So, for us - we don't need a different config that works with Wasabi right now - I've opened this to make you aware it "broke" and potentially needs "fixing" (revert to old behaviour), or docs to cover how to get this to work in a situation like this (including documenting which is the boundary version where this changes). . Thanks

Did you try the `--s3-no-check-bucket` flag? Which you can put into the config as `no_check_bucket = true`?

I'm pretty sure that will work around the problem

As to why...

The ultimate cause of this was a bug in rclone f8039deb7 which was letting bucket creation errors pass silently which is why it worked in 1.47.

This means that rclone now checks the return of the create bucket call. Attempting to create the bucket with a user with limited permissions is returning `AccessDenied` instead of `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou` or `BucketAlreadyExists`. Hence the need for the `no_check_bucket` permission.

I've added another paragraph to the docs with some more explanations: 3877df4e62dad93ef0309011896ae77262c22690

Sorry for the delay in coming back to this. I've now had a chance to test this and with v1.54.0 and ```no_check_bucket = true``` in the config this works as expected. 

I've tested this on v1.47.0 and it works on that too.  

So, yes Wasabi requires use of ```no_check_bucket = true``` even though this used to work without in <= 1.47.0

Many thanks for your help!

thanks for guys bringing it up, was crashing my head over the table, trying to understand WTH CreateBucket when I just copy file to Wasabi .
With config changes, it works fine now.

repository.description: Asynchronous MySQL Replication on Kubernetes using Percona Server and Openark's Orchestrator.

issue.body:
rclone always tries to create a bucket because of a bug.
As a mysql-cluster backup configuration, there is almost no incentive to have rclone create the bucket.
Therefore, enable the no_check_bucket option to make it more secure.
https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/4913
